key_insight: The ANGLE trial will test whether hyperangulated video laryngoscope blades improve first-attempt intubation success compared with standard-geometry blades.
clinical_relevance: Findings could inform blade selection for emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults.
method: Pragmatic, multicenter, unblinded, parallel-group randomized trial targeting 2,500 adults.
Conducted at 28 US sites: 10 emergency departments and 18 intensive care units.
Primary outcome: first-attempt intubation success; secondary outcome: hypoxemia during intubation.
evidence_signal: This protocol reports no outcome results; enrollment began December 30, 2025, and is expected to conclude in 2027.
watch_item: The unblinded design may allow operator expectations to influence procedural performance; this is not an AI study.
paper_title: Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for the Hyperangulated versus Standard Geometry Laryngoscope Blade (ANGLE) Trial
